Run, analyse and plot a Bayesian mixed model in one step

Source: R/bayes_mm.R
bayes_mm.Rd

A wrapper that runs a Bayesian mixed model (or takes one you have already run), prints a report of the model, and then plots all of the main effects and all of the interactions. It is the quickest way to analyse a data set; the functions it calls (bayes_mm_run(), bayes_mm_mainFX() and bayes_mm_interact()) can also be used on their own, for more control.

Usage

bayes_mm(bmm = list(), outp = "analysis", title = NULL, plotcheck = F, ...)

Arguments

bmm

A model that you have already run, either the output of bayes_mm_run() or the list returned by this function. If it is not given (the default), a new model is run using the arguments in ....

outp

The name of a folder in which to save the text report and the plots as pdfs (it is created if needed). Set to NULL or "" to not save anything.

title

Extra text to add to the plot titles and the report file name.

plotcheck

If TRUE, also return plots to check the model: the traces of the chains, a posterior check of the mean, and a posterior check of the density of the data.

...

Arguments for bayes_mm_run() (data, dvname, conditions, groups, binom, iter etc.) if a model is to be run, and/or for bayes_mm_mainFX(), bayes_mm_interact() and eyethinkdata::pirateye() for plotting.

Value

A list with:

bmm

the model (a stanreg object), which you can pass back to the plotting functions

mainFX

output of bayes_mm_mainFX()

interactFX

the plots from bayes_mm_interact(), or NULL if there was only one condition

plotcheck_plots

the check plots, if plotcheck = TRUE

param

the table of model parameters

Details

The report. The model, its priors, and a table of parameters (from parameters::model_parameters) are printed to the console, followed by the means and contrasts for the main effects and interactions. If outp is a folder name, the same text is also saved to a file in that folder called <dv> <conditions>BayesMM <title>.txt.

The plots. All the main effects are plotted by bayes_mm_mainFX(). If there is more than one condition, the interactions are plotted by bayes_mm_interact(): the first condition with each of the others, and then all of them together. The plots are drawn by eyethinkdata::pirateye(), and are saved as pdfs in the outp folder.

Passing arguments. If you supply bmm, everything in ... goes to the plotting functions, so you can use any argument of bayes_mm_mainFX(), bayes_mm_interact() or eyethinkdata::pirateye() (eg bars = TRUE). If you want bayes_mm() to run the model for you, then ... must contain the arguments for bayes_mm_run() (data, dvname, conditions, groups and so on); these are also passed to the plotting functions, which ignore them. Because bayes_mm_run() does not accept plotting arguments, it is best to run the model first with bayes_mm_run() if you want to customise the plots.

See also

bayes_mm_run(), bayes_mm_mainFX(), bayes_mm_interact()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
res <- bayes_mm(data = ad_data, dvname = "rating",
                conditions = c("adcon", "dim", "tv"), groups = "pid",
                plotcheck = TRUE)
# replot, using the model that was returned
bayes_mm_interact(res, interacts = "adcon:dim:tv", violin = FALSE)
} # }
